title: Swift Bharat 2026
description: Speakers, talks, schedule, tickets, and event updates for Swift Bharat 2026 in Mumbai.

items.title: Swift Bharat 2026 event guide
items.summary: Event details and the announced speaker lineup for Swift Bharat 2026.
items.content_text: Swift Bharat 2026 takes place on 19–20 November 2026 at Yashwantrao Chavan Centre in Mumbai. Announced speakers: Donny Wals — Indie Developer, Consultant, and Content Creator; Monika Mateska — Software engineer at RevenueCat and conference organizer; Marcin Krzyzanowski — Open source developer, building Notepad.exe, and senior engineer at Goodnotes; Hidde van der Ploeg — Better than Mustafa at everything; Natasha The Robot — Creator, writer, and community organizer; Nikhil Nigade — Indie iOS and macOS developer, designing delightful apps; Kanishka Chaudhry — iOS engineer at Upstox and Apple Scholar; Josh Holtz — Odd jobs at RevenueCat, lead maintainer of fastlane, and organizer of Deep Dish Swift; Ratnesh Jain — Indie developer building CommunityTalks. The provisional schedule is available: Day 1 runs 9:00 AM–5:00 PM IST and Day 2 runs 10:00 AM–5:00 PM IST. Speaker names for each session and talk titles will be announced soon. Tickets start at ₹4,999 and include all keynote sessions, lunch and refreshments, conference materials, and the post-conference mixer. Tentative evening plans: Day 1 — mixer + BEST buses; Day 2 — indie app fair + dinner. Both start at 5 PM. Day 1 wraps by 8:30 PM; Day 2 wraps by 8:30 PM and is only for conference attendees with apps, with no outside guests. Details to come!
items.content_html:
Swift Bharat 2026 takes place on 19–20 November 2026 at Yashwantrao Chavan Centre in Mumbai.

Announced speakers


Donny Wals — Indie Developer, Consultant, and Content Creator
Dabbawala-grade await: Donny wrote the book on Swift Concurrency. Mumbai’s dabbawalas deliver lakhs of lunches a day without a data race: every tiffin awaited, none lost. Stroopwafel for the flight from the Netherlands.


Monika Mateska — Software engineer at RevenueCat and conference organizer
Tree pose, green build: Monika codes and does yoga, sometimes at the same time. Balanced on one leg, laptop in one hand, build passing: peak work–life balance.


Marcin Krzyzanowski — Open source developer, building Notepad.exe, and senior engineer at Goodnotes
Locked and noted: CryptoSwift keeps a lot of apps’ secrets safe, and now he’s building Notepad.exe. So: a trusty brass padlock on a notepad full of code.


Hidde van der Ploeg — Better than Mustafa at everything
Mustafa’s Design Award: Hidde is the best at crafting delightful app experiences, and Mustafa’s favourite to win the design award (after a few others, obviously). So he gets the only cube that matters.


Natasha The Robot — Creator, writer, and community organizer
Powered by banana chips: Natasha has spent a good stretch of time in Kerala, out by the mangroves. Every robot needs fuel, and in Kerala that’s a paper cone of crispy banana chips.


Nikhil Nigade — Indie iOS and macOS developer, designing delightful apps
The original feed reader: Nikhil builds Elytra, a lovingly crafted RSS reader. Mumbai’s original feed still arrives by bicycle at 6 AM, tied with string.


Kanishka Chaudhry — iOS engineer at Upstox and Apple Scholar
Class of Swift: Kanishka is a Swift Student Challenge winner and Apple Scholar. Scholar cap on, diploma up, code on screen: ready to ship.


Josh Holtz — Odd jobs at RevenueCat, lead maintainer of fastlane, and organizer of Deep Dish Swift
Deep dish, fast lane: Josh maintains fastlane and runs Deep Dish Swift in Chicago. Nothing beats Mumbai traffic like an auto-rickshaw, and this one’s delivering deep dish.


Ratnesh Jain — Indie developer building CommunityTalks
Broadcasting from a Pi: Ratnesh runs Swift on a Raspberry Pi (ask him at his talk) and his CommunityTalks app is powered by one. So: Mumbai’s lamp-post loudspeaker, wired straight into a Pi.

The provisional schedule is available: Day 1 runs 9:00 AM–5:00 PM IST and Day 2 runs 10:00 AM–5:00 PM IST. Speaker names for each session and talk titles will be announced soon. Tickets start at ₹4,999 and include all keynote sessions, lunch and refreshments, conference materials, and the post-conference mixer. Tentative evening plans: Day 1 — mixer + BEST buses; Day 2 — indie app fair + dinner. Both start at 5 PM. Day 1 wraps by 8:30 PM; Day 2 wraps by 8:30 PM and is only for conference attendees with apps, with no outside guests. Details to come!
